newsitem.title: USA: Fed must be vigilant on inflation near-term - Meyer.
newsitem.headline: Fed must be vigilant on inflation near-term - Meyer.

text.p: Inflation has been exceptionally well behaved over the past year, even declining, and the Federal Reserve must do all it can to maintain that progress, Fed Governor Laurence Meyer said Sunday.

"In the near term, I believe we should be vigilant to insure that the progress made to lower inflation to the current level is sustained," Meyer said in remarks prepared for delivery to the National Association of Business Economists.
A text of his remarks was issued in advance in Washington.

"While I am focused on holding the line on inflation in the short run, I am also mindful of the importance of continuing progress toward price stability over the longer run and of the importance that current decisions be part of a longer strategic plan," Meyer said.

He said it has become difficult to say what constitutes a normal, non-inflationary rate of unemployment. A level of around six percent had been suggested in the past, yet current unemployment is below that and the country has enjoyed "stable to declining inflation over the past two years." Meyer noted.
He said that as a result of recent declining inflation, it may be the case normal unemployment can be as low 5-1/2 percent without risking a flare-up in inflation pressures.

"Tempering some of the optimism about NAIRU (non-accelerating inflationary rate of unemploment) and recent inflation is evidence of at least a modest acceleration in wages and compensation," Meyer said.

While that is a concern, there are still questions whether higher wages signal an upturn in price inflation, he noted. Some of it might simply be firms passing on to workers the slower increases they have incurred recently in benefit costs.

Nonetheless, Meyer cautioned it was important not to make "too many excuses" about rising wage costs and said that "developments related to wages, compensation and productivity deserve particular scrutiny."
On Friday, the Labor Department reported that unemployment in August dropped to a seven-year low of 5.1 percent from 5.4 percent in July as 244,000 new jobs were created.

It also said average hourly earnings rose six cents last month to $11.87 after falling two cents in July. Over the past year, hourly earnings have risen 3.6 percent, outpacing the 3 percent gain in consumer prices over the same period.
